chunks: Ali ibn al-Sindi from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the saying of Allah, Exalted is He: 'That is for those whose families are not present in the Sacred Mosque.' He said, 'That refers to the people of Mecca; they have no Mut'ah (temporary pilgrimage) and no Umrah is incumbent upon them.'
I said, 'So what is the boundary of that?' He said, 'Forty-eight miles from all sides of Mecca, excluding 'Usfan and excluding Dhat 'Irq.'

key_terms.مُتْعَةٌ: Mut'ah (a type of pilgrimage with a specified duration)

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'people of Mecca' exempt from Umrah according to Imam al-Sadiq, and what is their geographical boundary?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the Quranic exception for the residents of Mecca, clarifying that they are exempt from the obligation of Umrah and the specific Mut'ah pilgrimage rites due to their proximity to the Haram. He provides a precise geographical definition of this exemption, setting the boundary at forty-eight miles from Mecca in all directions, explicitly excluding the regions of 'Usfan and Dhat 'Irq. This narration highlights the scholarly tradition of linking legal rulings directly to the linguistic nuances of the Quranic text.
